subject: SDK guardrail: connection leak observed in VaultPay POC - need triage & short-term mitigation
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@vaultpay.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-09-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Odd connection behavior during high-concurrency run

Hi Sean,

Quick note from our POC run this morning: when we ramped concurrent chat streams to ~140 connections the Java SDK process started to hold sockets open and memory climbed steadily until we crashed an integration worker. We captured a heap snapshot and some logs — attaching. This is on SDK v1.4.2 (we used the NIO client).

Is there a recommended flag or a short-term workaround? We tried increasing the connection pool but it didn’t help. Happy to hop on a call.

Thanks,
Elena
VP Engineering
VaultPay

Attachments:
- trace-20280915.log (text)
- sdk-payload-sample.json (json)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Morales <elena@vaultpay.com>
Date: 2028-09-15T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Odd connection behavior during high-concurrency run

Folks — forwarding VaultPay's logs. Summary: SDK v1.4.2 (Java) with NIO client; memory and socket leak under sustained ~140 simultaneous chat streams. This POC is in our mid-enterprise funnel (DEAL-4821). Priority: customer-facing POC.

Quick asks:
- Karthik: can runtime team confirm whether the server-side keepalive/timeout interactions could be triggering unclosed channels?
- Logan: any recent client-side changes in connection reaper / connection pooling?
- Marissa: can we offer VaultPay a short-term demo flag or a patched SDK build while we triage?

I can join a triage call this afternoon.

—Sean
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Morales <elena@vaultpay.com>
Date: 2028-09-15T12:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Odd connection behavior during high-concurrency run

Thanks Sean — I pulled the logs. Initial impressions: we see lots of partial responses and many requests that never send a final FIN. Two hypotheses: (A) NIO client not draining the async response queue on backpressure leading to GC pressure and open file descriptors, or (B) a recent runtime change to streaming chunk boundary handling caused the client to retry low-level frames and leave sockets in CLOSE_WAIT.

Short-term asks for the field:
- Can VaultPay toggle client-side streaming mode to "sync-handoff" (a flag we added in 1.4.0) to reduce concurrency on the async path? That usually mitigates NIO edgecases.
- Please send a JVM thread dump and the heap-snapshot file (we saw a reference to it in Elena's attach list).

I can reproduce locally with a stress harness if someone can share the exact request cadence (messages/sec) and payload sizes. If the hypothesis points to runtime framing, we may need an internal patch to how we mark streams as completed.

Karthik
Senior Platform Engineer — Serving Runtime

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena@vaultpay.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-09-16T08:33:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Odd connection behavior during high-concurrency run

Elena — quick update from our side and a proposed short-term mitigation:

1) Please upload the heap-snapshot-20280916.txt (we only received the logs so far). That will speed root-cause.
2) Try starting the SDK with the environment variable REDWOOD_STREAMING_MODE=sync-handoff and disable the keepalive extension: -Dredwood.client.keepalive=false. That pairing has worked for one other customer with similar symptoms.
3) If that fails, we can ship a patched 1.4.3 build with an opt-in connection-reaper fix; I can get legal to approve a dev build for POC use (no SLA).

If you want a call, I'm free 10–11 PT today.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: heap-snapshot-20280916.txt (requested)

From: Elena Morales <elena@vaultpay.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-09-16T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Odd connection behavior during high-concurrency run

Marissa — thanks. Uploading the heap snapshot now and will restart their test harness using REDWOOD_STREAMING_MODE=sync-handoff + keepalive disabled; I'll report back in ~45m. We observed ~180 messages/sec per connection for 120 connections and payloads average ~1.8KB.

Attaching: heap-snapshot-20280916.txt (text)

—Elena

(On a side note: they have a tight go-live window; any chance of a temporary workaround in the console to throttle incoming streams per-token for dedicated customers?)

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Morales <elena@vaultpay.com>
Date: 2028-09-19T16:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Odd connection behavior during high-concurrency run

Quick update after reproducing with the stress harness: we see the client-side NIO selector holding sockets in CLOSE_WAIT when a particular mix of streaming payloads + intermittent backpressure happens. I pushed a candidate fix (PR #runtime/5678) that ensures when the client gives up on an in-flight streaming frame we explicitly drain and close the selector channel instead of leaving it to GC.

Planned next steps:
- Karthik: can you review runtime/5678 and if it looks sane we can cut a 1.4.3 RC for VaultPay.
- Marissa: if legal OKs a dev RC, we'll run the patched SDK in their POC tomorrow morning and monitor sockets.
- Sean: please relay that the mitigation is an opt-in RC; if REDWOOD_STREAMING_MODE=sync-handoff + keepalive=false works they can avoid the RC.

Log excerpt included inline in the PR. I'd mark this as high-priority for the runtime patching queue given multiple deals are on similar POC patterns.

—Logan Wright
Principal Engineer, SDK & Integrations
